title: Test-first and the agent roster
summary: Test-first work, an orchestrated session shape and a roster of planner, builder, verifier, adversary and adjudicator agents with the commands that drive them.
why: Fixes without a reproduction kept coming back, and work graded by its own author passed defects nobody could see. Separate roles with a failing test first keep both from happening.

items.title: Failing test first
items.does: Adds the rule: spec, then a test that fails for the right reason, then the smallest change, then the verification its tier needs.
items.why: A fix without a reproduction re-broke later; the failing test is what proves a change is about the bug.

items.title: Orchestrated, self-checking session shape
items.does: Adds the rule that one merger holds the plan, disjoint slices run in parallel worktrees, and every finding gets a refuting pass.
items.why: The merger's context stays small because the slices carry the detail, and a finding that survives a deliberate refutation is worth reporting.

items.title: Planner agent
items.does: Installs a planner agent that writes the spec and a slice plan with disjoint write-lists before any code.
items.why: Building on an assumption that a spec would have exposed is the most expensive way to find it.

items.title: Builder agent
items.does: Installs a builder agent that implements exactly one slice in its own worktree, test first, inside its write-list.
items.why: Disjoint slices are checked before dispatch rather than hoped for, so parallel builders never collide.

items.title: Verifier agent
items.does: Installs a verifier agent that re-runs the tests from a clean checkout and checks every cited file and claim.
items.why: A done claim is only as good as the evidence behind it; the verifier is that evidence and never edits.

items.title: Adversary agent
items.does: Installs an adversary agent that tries to refute one finding through one lens and says REFUTED when unsure.
items.why: Two agents agreeing is not evidence. A deliberate attempt to break a finding is.

items.title: Adjudicator agent
items.does: Installs an adjudicator agent that decides between candidates against stated criteria and records the call.
items.why: Acting without asking needs someone neutral to settle the real blocks, and a record so the call can be revisited.

items.title: Researcher agent
items.does: Installs a researcher agent that searches for prior art and checks each source's licence, without copying code in.
items.why: Third-party code arrives through a licence gate, not through a paste.

items.title: UI auditor agent
items.does: Installs a UI auditor agent that reviews changed screens for structure, typography, hit targets, characters and hierarchy.
items.why: Interface regressions are cheap to catch before a commit and costly to notice after a release.

items.title: Doc-sync agent
items.does: Installs a doc-sync agent that compares every restated fact in the markdown files with its one owning file.
items.why: A number restated in three files drifts in two of them; one owner per fact keeps them honest.

items.title: /orchestrated-run
items.does: Installs a command that runs recall, plan, parallel builders, the verifier gate and the merge as one entry point.
items.why: One command makes the session shape the easy path instead of a checklist to remember.

items.title: /root-cause-fix
items.does: Installs a command for bugs: reproduction test first, every sibling occurrence of the cause, the minimal fix, and a backfill of data the bug already damaged.
items.why: Bugs came back through sibling code paths with the same shape, and fixed code left corrupted rows behind.

items.title: /diagnose
items.does: Installs a five-step debugging command: reproduce, minimise, hypothesise, fix one thing, verify.
items.why: An investigation without a loop flails: it changes several things at once and cannot say which one helped.

items.title: superpowers plugin (listed only)
items.does: Names the superpowers plugin from the official marketplace: skills for test-driven work, planning, worktrees, verification and review.
items.why: The author's sessions invoke these packaged disciplines constantly. Installing a plugin is your own act, so the profile only lists it.
items.notes: Install it yourself from the official plugin marketplace; nothing is installed here.

items.title: Playwright plugin (listed only)
items.does: Names the Playwright plugin, which drives a browser for interface checks and end-to-end tests.
items.why: Interface read-backs need a real browser; this is the one the author uses for them.
items.notes: Listed with its reason; you install it from the marketplace if you want it.

items.title: Chrome DevTools plugin (listed only)
items.does: Names the Chrome DevTools plugin for accessibility, performance and network audits.
items.why: Accessibility and performance audits catch interface faults that a screenshot does not show.
items.notes: The profile never installs plugins; marketplace installs stay your decision.

items.title: Same-day work on worktree branches
items.does: Adds the rule that versions and multi-step builds live on a worktree branch and reach main only by a fast-forward once verified.
items.why: Late edits on main broke tools that read it, and a public project should not see every intermediate version.

items.title: Shared rule file for every agent
items.does: Creates .claude/session-default.md with the shape, hard rules, progress contract and verdict lines, which every agent definition reads first.
items.why: Sub-agents do not inherit the main session's CLAUDE.md; one shared file beats restating the rules in eight agent files.

items.title: Size cap per agent file
items.does: Adds the rule that each agent definition stays under the agent file budget, which the budget checker enforces.
items.why: Agent files load into every dispatch, so each extra kilobyte is paid on every sub-agent call.

items.title: Recall before the spec
items.does: Adds phase 0: before planning, read the hand-off, history, roadmap, rulings and memory; a CLOSED or REFUTED hit stops the work.
items.why: Work that had already been closed or refuted was being built a second time; reading first is cheaper than building twice.

items.title: Review depth scaled by risk
items.does: Adds the rule that diffs touching core logic get the full adversary lens set, plumbing gets one lens, and refute rounds are capped before the adjudicator decides.
items.why: Full adversarial review on every small plumbing change spent most of the review budget where defects were least likely.

items.title: No agent grades its own work
items.does: Adds the rule that the producer of a slice, spec or candidate is never its verifier, adversary or adjudicator.
items.why: Self-grading passed exactly the defects the producer could not see.

items.title: Claims check for multi-builder rounds
items.does: Installs claims_check.py: the verifier lists the files, absences and counts a report claims, and the tool re-measures each one and refuses on the first that does not hold.
items.why: A replayed tool output once reported fabricated counts. Enable it once several builders report in one round; the verifier alone covers most work.

items.title: Model and effort chosen by run kind
items.does: Adds the routing rule: planning on the strongest model, fixes on a mid-size one, verification and inbox replies on a mid-size model at low effort.
items.why: Running every background job on the top model spent most of the budget on acknowledgements. Enable it once headless spend matters to you.

items.title: Each lane owns its paths
items.does: Creates .claude/lanes.json, a registry of the paths each background lane may write, with shared directories listed explicitly.
items.why: Two lanes editing one file collided before file claims existed; a path registry makes the boundary visible up front. Useful only with parallel lanes.

items.title: Director, auditor and executor roles
items.does: Adds the loop rule that the director and auditor run read-only in plan mode, only the executor changes files, and cycles are capped.
items.why: Separating planning from execution kept an autonomous loop from approving its own work. It is for heavy users once background lanes are proven.
